subject: Film & Cinema
title: Film Financing: Following the Money
description: A 60-second lesson on Film Financing: Following the Money.

hook.text: A Hollywood blockbuster can cost $300 million. Where does all that money come from?

buildup.text: Studios fund tentpoles. Independent films use private investors, tax incentives, and pre-sales.

discovery.text: Pre-selling international distribution rights can finance an entire film before shooting starts.

twist.text: Hollywood accounting is designed so even profitable films can officially show a loss.

climax.text: Understanding film finance reveals why certain movies get made and others never will.

punchline.text: In Hollywood, the budget tells the real story.

quiz.question: What is 'pre-selling' in film financing?
options: Selling distribution rights before the film is made to fund production
